newsitem.title: USA: N. Calif. transit agencies consider toll lanes.
newsitem.headline: N. Calif. transit agencies consider toll lanes.

text.p: Northern California transportation officials on Monday said they would consider building toll lanes along Highway 101 to reduce traffic congestion.

The Sonoma County Transportation Authority and the Metropolitan Transportation Commission said they would sponsor a feasibility study to determine if the proposed "variable-priced" toll lanes would raise enough revenue to pay for construction and cover related costs.
The study will consider a plan to build the toll lanes in Sonoma County along 22 miles of state Route 101, one of California's main north-south highways.
The study, which is expected to take nine months to complete, will assess the demand for the toll lanes and the potential cost of the project.
If the study concludes that the toll lanes are feasible, local official could then seek state legislative approval.
Proponents of the project say newly constructed toll roads in Orange County, Calif., have reduced congestion, and that toll lanes in Sonoma would have a similar benefit.
